paragraphs: Friend, look at how this whole thing started. Ezra is facedown, weeping over sin that was not even about him alone, and a crowd gathers and weeps too. Then Shecaniah says, "We have been unfaithful to our God…" (Ezra 10:2), and notice he says WE, yet he still says, "…there is hope for Israel." (Ezra 10:2) Real confession doesn't point fingers or hide, it tells the truth and keeps hope in the same breath.

Now, this passage is heavy, and I think that last line about children hurts. I'm not going to pretty it up, and I'm not going to guess past what the text says. What it does show is that when they saw they had been unfaithful, they didn't shrug or say "circle back next week," they showed up, took an oath, and priests brought a guilt offering (Ezra 10:5, 10:19). Being sorry and doing something about it go together.

So here's what I'd bake into your day, friend. God's Word can show you something that needs to change, and that moment is not the time to hide or make excuses. Say it plainly, own it, and take the next step. I've been in a dusty drawer, so trust me, being honest about where you are is where the way out begins.
